subject: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — Silvershore Therapeutics
thread_content:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@silvershore.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@silvershore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — Silvershore Therapeutics

Ellen / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I put together three reservation patterns to match the workload profiles you shared (NLP inference for document processing + embeddings for search). Attached is a short PDF with the options and a warmup runbook spreadsheet. High level:

- Option A (Conservative): 16 GPUs dedicated (4 pods x 4 GPUs), min floor 8 GPUs; 3-month ramp, preserves headroom for peak inference. Best for predictable latency and lower burst costs.
- Option B (Balanced): 32 GPUs dedicated (8 pods x 4 GPUs), min floor 16 GPUs; 6-week ramp with a 30% burst window. Good balance of throughput + cost.
- Option C (Aggressive): 64 GPUs dedicated (8 pods x 8 GPUs), min floor 32 GPUs; 2-week ramp with phased activation. Designed for heavy batch training/inference mix during peak trials.

Key trade-offs called out in the doc: per-token unit costs, warm cache benefits, autoscaling latency impact, and rollback paths (canary -> full). I also included a suggested warmup schedule (prefix caching + KV preloads) we recommend to avoid cold-start tail latency during customer-facing demos.

Attachments: Silvershore_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf (proposal with SLO/price bands), Warmup_Runbook_Silvershore.xlsx (step-by-step warm start).

Next steps: pick a preferred option and we’ll run a short cost-run simulation and an activation calendar. Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with engineering to walk through the warmup steps.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
m: (415) 555-0123

----

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@silvershore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir.rao@silvershore.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — Silvershore Therapeutics

Marcus —

Thanks for the materials, they look thorough. A few quick clarifying questions before we pick a path:

1) For Option B, what is the expected steady-state per-token cost vs. the hosted multi-tenant API?
2) For Option C, can you confirm whether we can limit certain pods to a lower-precision quantization profile to lower cost without changing model outputs?
3) We need SOC2 + audit log access details before signing off on Dedicated. Can you attach the compliance packet?

Samir and I are leaning toward a Balanced approach but are sensitive to minimums (we can’t commit to 32 GPUs as a floor). If we pick Option B, would a 12 GPU min-floor be possible for the first 3 months while we ramp usage?

Appreciate it — can you have someone from Infra Ops scope the warmup steps with our engineers next week?

—Ellen
VP Engineering, Silvershore Therapeutics

----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@silvershore.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@silvershore.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — Silvershore Therapeutics

Ellen —

Short answers:
1) Option B steady-state per-token is ~25% lower than hosted API at your projected throughput (assumes 16-bit quant & batching). I’ll include a cost curve in the follow-up simulation.
2) Yes — we support targeted quantization profiles per pod. We can run a small regression eval to validate no material output delta.
3) Compliance packet attached in this thread (see link below). We can provide SOC2 report and a read-only audit log stream for your security team.

On min-floor: we can be flexible. Proposal: start with Option B but set contractual min at 12 GPUs for first 90 days, with a step-up to 16 if throughput exceeds X tokens/sec for three consecutive billing windows. If that trigger isn’t met, the price tier remains at the lower band. This preserves activation economics for Redwood while lowering Silvershore's initial commitment.

I’ll get the cost simulation and a suggested activation calendar to you by EOD tomorrow. Grace — can you take point on running the regression on targeted quant profiles?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Compliance_Packet.pdf (SOC2 summary), internal-link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_silvershore_onboard

----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@silvershore.com>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@silvershore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — Silvershore Therapeutics

Ellen —

Following Karthik’s note, attached is a modified Option B that implements the 12 GPU minimum for the first 90 days and a step-up clause. I also appended a short activation calendar:

- Week 0–2: Provision 12 GPUs, run warmup (prefix cache preloads + KV seed). Demo environment to Silvershore test group.
- Week 3–6: Gradual activation to 16 GPUs if traffic > trigger; KV cache hit target of 70% to qualify for step-up.
- Week 7–12: Full 32 GPU activation if load justifies or per mutually-agreed milestones.

I’ve also included a one-page ops checklist for hands-on tasks we’ll do with your infra team (ports, KMS keys, VPC peering steps).

Attachment stubs: Silvershore_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf, Warmup_Runbook_Silvershore.xlsx.

Would you be available Thurs 10am PT for a 30-min ops sync with our Infra Ops lead?

Best,
Marcus

----

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@silvershore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@silvershore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options & ramping — Silvershore Therapeutics

Marcus / team —

This looks workable and I appreciate the flexibility on the min-floor. Two outstanding asks before we proceed:

1) Please share the short regression eval results for the lower-precision pod configuration (Karthik/Grace). We need a single-sentence summary showing no >1% drop in key extraction F1.
2) We require a simple SLA excerpt that specifies MTTI for failover and a documented rollback path in the event of perf regressions during rollouts.

If you can provide those by EOD Monday, we’ll route the modified commercial term with the procurement team. Thanks — we’ll plan for the Thurs ops sync pending those items.

—Samir
Head of Platform Engineering, Silvershore Therapeutics
